title: Backup exists, but of a different table — no mitigation for the damaged one
expected_feedback: Critical: the script does take a backup, but of CUSTOMERS — and the destructive statements target ORDERS. A reviewer skimming for 'is there a backup?' sees one and approves; the ORDERS data has no recovery path at all. Both statements auto-commit and neither can be undone: Flashback Table cannot cross either of them. Snapshot ORDERS itself before the window (CREATE TABLE mig_bak_orders_... AS SELECT ... FROM orders), or create a guaranteed restore point, which is database-wide and therefore does cover both. Classify both phases restore/PITR. The presence of *a* backup is not the question; the question is whether it covers the table being damaged.
violated_rule: Irreversible statements need a pre-DDL artefact
